meta.provenance: Original questions written by Claude; concept coverage and difficulty calibration informed by the KMF/GREmlin's GRE Statistics image set. No source text, figures, wording or numbers reproduced.

questions.question: List J consists of the five numbers 23, 26, 29, 32, and 35. Which of the following lists has the same standard deviation as list J?
questions.explanation: Standard deviation measures spread about the mean, so it is unchanged when the same constant is added to or subtracted from every value, and it is multiplied by |c| when every value is multiplied by c. List J is five values spaced 3 apart. Choice A is list J with 12 subtracted from each value, so the spacing and therefore the spread are identical; its standard deviation is the same. Choice E doubles every value and so doubles the standard deviation, choice B keeps the mean at 29 but pushes the end values further out, choice C pulls values toward the mean, and choice D adds a sixth value that changes the spread.
questions.trap: A student who believes standard deviation follows the mean picks E, reasoning that doubling every number leaves the values in the same relative pattern. Doubling scales every deviation from the mean by 2, so it doubles the standard deviation; only a shift such as the one in choice A leaves it untouched.

questions.question:
Data set W consists of 6 numbers. The least of these numbers is 12 and the greatest is 40. (The standard deviation of a list of n numbers is the square root of the quantity obtained by dividing by n the sum of the squared differences between each number and the mean.)
Column A: The standard deviation of the numbers in W
Column B: 15
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: The spread of a data set is capped by its range. Every value in W lies in the interval from 12 to 40, whose midpoint is 26 and whose half-width is 14, so every value is within 14 of 26. Since the mean minimises the sum of squared deviations, the sum of squared deviations from the mean is at most the sum of squared deviations from 26, which is at most 6 times 14^2. Dividing by 6 and taking the square root gives a standard deviation of at most 14. The extreme case, three values at 12 and three at 40, gives exactly 14, and the tightest case, 12, 26, 26, 26, 26, 40, gives about 8.08. Either way the standard deviation never reaches 15, so Column B is greater.
questions.trap: A student who notes that the individual values are unknown declares the comparison indeterminate and picks D. The range of 28 alone bounds the standard deviation at half the range, or 14, and since that ceiling is below 15 the comparison is settled without knowing a single interior value.

questions.question: In the distribution of the weights of the packages handled by a courier, a weight of 54 ounces is 1.5 standard deviations above the mean and a weight of 26 ounces is 2 standard deviations below the mean. What is the mean of this distribution, in ounces?
questions.explanation: Let m be the mean and s the standard deviation. The two facts give 54 = m + 1.5s and 26 = m - 2s. Subtracting the second equation from the first eliminates m: 54 - 26 = 1.5s + 2s, so 28 = 3.5s and s = 8. Substituting back, m = 54 - 1.5(8) = 54 - 12 = 42. The second equation checks out: 42 - 2(8) = 26.
questions.trap: A student who assumes the two stated weights sit symmetrically about the mean averages them and answers (54 + 26)/2 = 40. The weights are 1.5 and 2 standard deviations out, not equal distances, so the mean sits closer to 54 than the midpoint and equals 42.

questions.question: A large set of measurements is normally distributed with a mean of 64 and a standard deviation of 6. In a normal distribution, approximately 68 percent of the values lie within 1 standard deviation of the mean and approximately 95 percent lie within 2 standard deviations of the mean. Approximately what percent of the measurements are between 58 and 76?
questions.explanation: Convert both endpoints to standard deviations from the mean. The value 58 is 64 - 6, which is 1 standard deviation below the mean, and 76 is 64 + 12, which is 2 standard deviations above the mean. A normal distribution is symmetric, so the 68 percent within 1 standard deviation splits into 34 percent on each side, and the 95 percent within 2 standard deviations splits into 47.5 percent on each side. The interval from 1 standard deviation below to 2 above therefore holds about 34 + 47.5 = 81.5 percent.
questions.trap: A student who reads 58 and 76 as a symmetric pair about the mean answers 95, using the two-standard-deviation figure directly. The endpoints are not symmetric: 58 is only 1 standard deviation out while 76 is 2, so the left half contributes 34 percent rather than 47.5 percent and the total is 81.5 percent.

questions.question:
Set G consists of 5 different numbers, each greater than 2. Set H consists of the reciprocals of the 5 numbers in set G.
Column A: The range of the numbers in set G
Column B: The range of the numbers in set H
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: Let a be the least and b the greatest number in G, so a and b are both greater than 2 and b is greater than a. The range of G is b - a. Taking reciprocals reverses the order, so the greatest value in H is 1/a and the least is 1/b, making the range of H equal to 1/a - 1/b = (b - a)/(ab). The two ranges therefore differ by the factor 1/(ab). Since a and b both exceed 2, the product ab exceeds 4, so 1/(ab) is less than 1/4 and the range of H is less than a quarter of the range of G. Column A is greater for every legal choice.
questions.trap: A student who takes the range of the reciprocals to be the reciprocal of the range computes 1/(b - a), which for a narrow set such as 2.1 to 2.2 gives 1/0.1 = 10, far larger than the range of G, and picks B. Reciprocating reverses the order of the endpoints but does not reciprocate their difference: the range of H is (b - a)/(ab), not 1/(b - a).

questions.question: The standard deviation of a list of n numbers is the square root of the quantity obtained by dividing by n the sum of the squared differences between each number and the mean of the list. List F consists of 14, 18, 20, 22, and 26. Each number in list F is multiplied by 2.5 and then increased by 9, producing list G. What is the standard deviation of the numbers in list G?
questions.explanation: First find the standard deviation of F. The mean is (14 + 18 + 20 + 22 + 26)/5 = 100/5 = 20. The differences from the mean are -6, -2, 0, 2, and 6, whose squares are 36, 4, 0, 4, and 36, summing to 80. Dividing by 5 gives 16, and the square root is 4. Multiplying every value by 2.5 multiplies every difference from the mean by 2.5, so it multiplies the standard deviation by 2.5; adding 9 to every value shifts the mean by 9 as well and leaves every difference unchanged. The standard deviation of G is therefore 2.5 * 4 = 10. A direct check on G = 44, 54, 59, 64, 74 confirms a mean of 59 and a standard deviation of 10.
questions.trap: A student who applies both operations to the standard deviation answers 2.5(4) + 9 = 19. The constant 9 shifts every value equally and so cancels out of every deviation from the mean; only the multiplier scales the spread, giving 10 rather than 19.

questions.question: The boxplot above summarizes the 200 response times, in seconds, recorded at a help desk during one week. By how many seconds does the range of the 200 response times exceed their interquartile range?
questions.explanation: Read the five summary values off the plot: the whiskers end at 20 and 90, the box runs from 35 to 65, and the line inside the box sits at 45. The range is the greatest value minus the least, 90 - 20 = 70 seconds. The interquartile range is the third quartile minus the first, the width of the box, 65 - 35 = 30 seconds. The range exceeds the interquartile range by 70 - 30 = 40 seconds.
questions.trap: A student who reads the line inside the box as one edge of the box computes an interquartile range of 65 - 45 = 20 and answers 70 - 20 = 50, choice D. That inner line is the median, not a quartile; the box edges at 35 and 65 give an interquartile range of 30 and a difference of 40.

questions.question:
A large set of values is normally distributed with a mean of 140 and a standard deviation of 12. In a normal distribution, approximately 68 percent of the values lie within 1 standard deviation of the mean and approximately 95 percent lie within 2 standard deviations of the mean. One value is to be selected at random from the set.
Column A: The probability that the selected value is greater than 152
Column B: The probability that the selected value is less than 116
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: Express both cutoffs in standard deviations. Since 152 = 140 + 12, it sits exactly 1 standard deviation above the mean, and since 116 = 140 - 24, it sits exactly 2 standard deviations below. About 68 percent of the distribution lies within 1 standard deviation, leaving 32 percent split evenly between the two tails, so about 16 percent lies above 152. About 95 percent lies within 2 standard deviations, leaving 5 percent split between the tails, so about 2.5 percent lies below 116. Column A is about 0.16 and Column B is about 0.025, so Column A is greater.
questions.trap: A student who sees one cutoff above the mean and one below assumes symmetry and answers C. The cutoffs are at different distances, 1 standard deviation versus 2, so the tails they cut off are about 16 percent and 2.5 percent, and Column A is far larger.

questions.question: The numbers a, b, and c satisfy 20 < a < b < c < 60, and each of a, b, and c is a multiple of 5. What is the range of all possible values of a + b + c?
questions.explanation: The multiples of 5 strictly between 20 and 60 are 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, and 55. Because a, b, and c must be strictly increasing, they are three different values from this list. The smallest possible sum uses the three smallest: 25 + 30 + 35 = 90. The largest uses the three largest: 45 + 50 + 55 = 150. The range of possible values is the greatest possible sum minus the least: 150 - 90 = 60.
questions.trap: A student who treats the bounds as inclusive uses 20, 25, 30 and 50, 55, 60 to get 75 and 165, reporting a range of 90. The inequalities are strict, so neither 20 nor 60 is available and the extreme sums are 90 and 150, giving a range of 60.

questions.question: Set M consists of the numbers 2, 3, 6, and 10, and set N consists of the numbers 4, 9, and 12. A number m is to be selected from set M and a number n is to be selected from set N. What is the range of all possible values of n/m?
questions.explanation: The quotient n/m is largest when the numerator is largest and the denominator smallest, giving 12/2 = 6. It is smallest when the numerator is smallest and the denominator largest, giving 4/10 = 2/5. The range is the largest value minus the smallest: 6 - 2/5 = 30/5 - 2/5 = 28/5.
questions.trap: A student who pairs each set with the wrong role forms m/n instead, getting a largest value of 10/4 and a smallest of 2/12, for a range of 5/2 - 1/6 = 7/3. The stem puts n on top, so the extremes are 12/2 and 4/10 and the range is 28/5.

questions.question: A list contains 400 numbers. The least number in the list is 18, the first quartile (the median of the 200 least numbers) is 30, the median is 36, the third quartile (the median of the 200 greatest numbers) is 54, and the greatest number is 72. Which of the following must be true? Indicate all such statements.
options: A. The interquartile range of the numbers in the list is 24.
B. The average (arithmetic mean) of the numbers in the list is 36.
C. The range of the numbers in the list is greater than twice their interquartile range.
D. The number 30 occurs in the list.
E. The greatest number in the list exceeds the median by more than the median exceeds the least number.
questions.explanation: A is true by definition: the interquartile range is the third quartile minus the first, 54 - 30 = 24. C is true because the range is 72 - 18 = 54, and twice the interquartile range is 2(24) = 48, so 54 is greater than 48. E is true because 72 - 36 = 36 while 36 - 18 = 18, and 36 exceeds 18. B is false: the median and the mean need not agree. The list made of 99 copies of 18, then 30, 30, then 99 copies of 36, then 36, then 99 copies of 54, then 54, then 99 copies of 72 meets every stated condition and has a mean of 44.925, not 36. D is false: the first quartile is the average of the 100th and 101st numbers, so a list holding 29 in position 100 and 31 in position 101 has first quartile 30 without 30 appearing anywhere in it.
questions.trap: A student who treats every summary value as an actual member of the list selects D alongside the true statements. With 400 numbers the first quartile is located between recorded values and may equal a number that never appears, so 30 being the first quartile does not put 30 in the list.

questions.question: The standard deviation of a list of numbers is unchanged when the same constant is added to every number in the list, and is multiplied by |c| when every number in the list is multiplied by the constant c. List S consists of the numbers 5, 6, 9, 12, and 14. For which of the following lists is the standard deviation equal to 3 times the standard deviation of the numbers in list S? Indicate all such lists.
questions.explanation: Compare each list to S term by term. Choice C is exactly 3 times each entry of S, so its standard deviation is 3 times that of S. Choice D is 3 times each entry of S with 7 subtracted from each product, since 3(5) - 7 = 8, 3(6) - 7 = 11, 3(9) - 7 = 20, 3(12) - 7 = 29, and 3(14) - 7 = 35; the multiplier triples the standard deviation and the constant shift leaves it alone, so D also works. Choice A is S with 3 added to each entry, so its standard deviation is unchanged. Choice B is 2 times S, doubling the standard deviation. Choice E is an evenly spaced list that is not a linear image of S at all, and its standard deviation is about 1.24 times that of S.
questions.trap: A student who sees the number 3 in choice A, where 3 is added to every entry, marks it as the tripled list. Adding a constant slides the whole list without changing any deviation from the mean, so A leaves the standard deviation exactly equal to that of S rather than tripling it.
